chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ubayd Allah al-Muwasawi from Ubayd Allah ibn Nahik from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a woman upon whom two witnesses testified that her husband had died, so she married another man, and then her first husband returned. He said: 'She is entitled to the dowry because of what he made permissible of her private part [by the second husband], and the two witnesses are flogged with the legal punishment and are liable for the dowry because they deceived the man. Then she observes the waiting period and returns to her first husband.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a husband returns after his wife married another man based on witnesses testifying to his death?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudence of *gharar* (deception) in marital status, establishing that the second husband retains the dowry as compensation for his lawful use of the woman's private part, while the witnesses bear financial liability for their false testimony. The ruling emphasizes the procedural necessity of the *iddah* (waiting period) before the woman fully reverts to her first husband, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise evidentiary standards in family law. This case study is frequently cited in *usul al-fiqh* to discuss the validity of single-witness versus two-witness testimonies in presumptive death cases.
